summary:
Sept 11, 1973_ 


I’m glad Leslie Flood had my address to give you ... I recall his reviews of my books back in the early ’50s. Nothing could make me happier than to know that you liked my Vancouver speech; I worked on it as long as I have some nov­ els—I was very blue and depressed at the time I wrote it, and so I put into it all I had left in my head in the way of ideas. It is, oddly, the first speech I ever wrote or gave. I got two reactions on it: 
(one) Sir, you are cold and cynical toward women and regard them merely as objects. 

(two) Sir, you have a sentimental attitude toward women and expect them as superior beings to solve all man’s problems while man just sits back. 

Oddly, both reactions were by women. Well, they will have to work it out for themselves. I guess to love a woman is now an insult to her—it makes her into a sex object—and if you don’t, well, then there is little joy in the world, just a lot of angry ladies catching you up at every slip of the tongue/pen. I have one novel going into galleys with no foreign contractual ties, called CON­ FESSIONS OF A CRAP ARTIST, but it is not science-fiction. And it certainly isn’t porno, despite the tide; it is an experimental novel, being published stricdy as a literary novel. Would you be interested in that.71 think it’s a good one.
